explanation: Matches the first question on erdosproblems.com/1054 and its resolution: f(n) = o(n) is false (Tao). The definition of f takes the least m with n = Σ_{i<k} (i-th smallest divisor of m) for some k ≥ 1. Nat.nth returns 0 past the last divisor, which only appends zeros, and undefined n get the junk value 0. That junk cannot make the negated statement easier, since Tao's bound gives f(n) > δn on a set of positive upper density of represented n.
